newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse strongly ahead.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse strongly ahead.

text.p: German shares advanced strongly in early bourse trade on Friday, supported by a strong dollar and firm German bonds and shrugging off a slide on Wall Street overnight.
Dealers said they were keeping one eye on the "triple-witching" options expiry due at around 1220 GMT.

Triple-witchings occur quarterly and involve the simultaneous expiry of DTB DAX futures contracts, DAX options and options on individual DAX stocks. They often increase volatility in the cash markets.
The DAX index stood at 3,288.39 points, up 23.72 points or 0.73 percent in early bourse, off an early high of 3,294.19 points.
"We expect the market to trade around the 3,300 point level. The dollar is supportive, and the debt market is also helping us along," said one Frankfurt trader.
Thursday's post-bourse fall was largely attributed to comments by U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan which market players interpreted as pointing to a possible interest rate hike in the U.S. soon.
"Fears about an interest rate hike either here or in the U.S. have mostly been discounted by now," the trader said.
The main feature of early trade was Deutsche Telekom AG, which was up 1.10 marks, around three percent, at 37.95 marks in bourse.
Dealers said that the market was focusing on Telekom as the share, which was floated in November, had been neglected somewhat during the recent record run for DAX blue-chip stocks.
